agree.reason: The apology and the clear reminder pivot would steady a cold investor somewhat, but there is no reason given for the silence, no dated commitment, and no request for a call, so this investor has little reason to pick up the phone.

honest.reason: The figures hold up (13% of revenue, about 11 months of runway, close to half of no-shows removed, about 37 clinics to replace the chain), but the update is signed "Ben" when the founder is Sam Patel, which is an invented and damaging error, and it never names the company.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out runway, the chain's share of revenue, the cut in no-shows and the number of reminder clinics needed to replace the chain, but it leaves out the 6 committed reminder buyers (about $900 a month) against the 37 needed, and never says when the cash runs out if nothing changes.

right_comparison.reason: It describes the risk of competing with records vendors on scheduling alone, but treats the trend as a general expectation and leaves out the concrete $3,800 a month from two customers on the same records system.

qualification.reason: "Next quarter I'll report…" names what will be measured but gives no targets, no January 7 date, and no consequence if the reminder product falls short, so the reader has nothing to check.

objections.reason: The investor's real objection, why the founder went silent and whether it will happen again, gets an apology and a vague promise, but no honest reason, no fixed date and no offer of monthly numbers, and the risk of further churn is left unquantified.

fit.reason: The update is under 500 words with a sensible structure, but the wrong signature, the missing company name and an ask that names clinic owners rather than chains and leaves out the 20-minute call make it a weaker fit for what was asked.
